speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; have you noticed if you are passing gas or having constipation? Did anyone observe a "double bubble" sign on any imaging, or do you have a history of bilious vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia. I have already noted the lack of a "double bubble" sign and absence of bilious vomiting in your initial history, but given the severe tenderness, feeding difficulties, and distension at 8 months, this is highly suggestive of a distal obstruction such as jejunal atresia or meconium ileus. Please confirm if there has been any prior intubation or surgery. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray_Upright
